Source: Kucherov Wants To Play With McDavid, Matthews Or Pastrnak Daria Tuboltseva Hockey Reporter Fact checked by: Sergey Demidov Updated: Nov 2, 2026, 1:30 p.m. Published: Nov 2, 2026, 1:30 p.m. 7 min read Editorial Standards Why Trust Us? Nikita Kucherov wants to win the scoring title every season and do it alongside Connor McDavid, Auston Matthews or David Pastrnak in a market big enough to keep him in the spotlight, an NHL source told RG.org. "Playing in Florida, people forget about you from time to time," the source said, days after the reigning Hart Trophy winner told the Tampa Bay Lightning he will not re-sign and asked for a trade. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) Nikita Kucherov's request to leave the Tampa Bay Lightning is about more than money, according to an NHL source who spoke to RG.org on condition of anonymity. The source said the 33-year-old forward wants to lead the league in scoring every year. He also wants to do it on a team with Connor McDavid, Auston Matthews or David Pastrnak, in a market large enough to keep him in the conversation. “He wants to be the top scorer every year and play on a team with McDavid or Matthews or Pastrnak, plus in a big market, so people talk about how good he is,” the source told RG. “Playing in Florida, people forget about you from time to time.” A Superstar Teammate And A Bigger Stage Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Friday that Kucherov told his teammates and the organization he will not sign another contract with Tampa Bay and would like to be traded. According to ESPN , he delivered the news to teammates before the team landed in Nashville. ESPN's Emily Kaplan also reported that Kucherov wants to play with another of the league's top stars and has specific players and teams in mind. The source who spoke to RG.org said Kucherov's view of the Lightning has shifted as well. “He understands that Tampa has already squeezed everything out of itself and you can’t win there,” the source said. “The team is average on its own.” Kucherov was central to Tampa Bay's back-to-back Stanley Cups in 2020 and 2021, but the club has not won a playoff series since beating the New York Rangers in the 2022 Eastern Conference Final. Last spring, the Lightning lost to the Montreal Canadiens in seven games in the first round. Money is also a factor. Chris Johnston reported earlier this fall that Kucherov's camp was seeking six years at $20 million per season. The Fourth Period's David Pagnotta reported chatter that the Lightning offered four years at about $15 million per season. The NHL salary cap is set to rise from $104 million this season to $113.5 million in 2027-28. Toronto Seen As The Realistic Landing Spot Of the three stars the source named, Matthews is the one Kucherov could realistically join, the source said. The source added that it would not happen through a deal with Tampa Bay. "Toronto is the more realistic option," the source said. "Not a trade. He will just go there in the summer." Kucherov is in the final season of an eight-year, $76 million contract with a $9.5 million cap hit and can become an unrestricted free agent on July 1, 2027. The deal includes a modified no-trade clause that allows him to submit a list of 10 teams he would accept a trade to. On Sportsnet's Saturday Headlines, Friedman said the Maple Leafs and Canadiens could interest Kucherov if Tampa Bay chose to move him and either team built an acceptable package, calling them two teams "among many he would consider." Friedman added that he could not confirm which teams are on the approved list. Matthews, the Maple Leafs' captain, is signed through 2027-28 and opened this season with eight goals and 18 points in his first 11 games. Toronto also has Kirill Marchenko, who shares an agent with Kucherov in Dan Milstein. A trade during the season would require the Leafs to send assets to an Atlantic Division rival and clear room on their 2027-28 payroll. A free-agent signing would require only the cap space. Lightning Say No Trade Is Coming General manager Julien BriseBois answered the reports Friday night with a statement posted by the team saying the Lightning have no intention of trading Kucherov. In September, BriseBois said both sides wanted a deal done and that he remained in contact with Milstein, with the goal of keeping Kucherov in Tampa for years. Coach Jon Cooper said Saturday that nothing has changed in the team's goals for this season. "Kuch is 100% a part of this team," Cooper said before the game in Nashville. Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic reported that Kucherov plans to keep playing while the situation plays out. Milstein indicated on social media that it is unlikely his client will stop suiting up, unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin after their recent trade requests. Kucherov was in the lineup that night and assisted on three of Tampa Bay's four goals in a 5-4 shootout loss to the Predators. Former Lightning captain Steven Stamkos scored the shootout winner. Kucherov has four goals and 14 assists for 18 points in 13 games this season for the Lightning (8-3-2). On Oct. 24, Kucherov passed Stamkos as the franchise's all-time leading scorer. He has 1,142 points (405 goals, 737 assists) in 892 regular-season games over 13 NHL seasons, all with Tampa Bay, plus 177 points in 159 playoff games. Last season he finished with 130 points (44 goals, 86 assists) in 76 games and won the Hart Trophy for the second time. He has reached 100 points in each of the past four seasons. Tampa Bay hosts the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday. Daria Tuboltseva has worked as a sports journalist since 2014 and has specialized in hockey coverage since 2016. She’s reported from some of the world’s biggest sporting events, including the Olympic Games (Beijing 2022), the FIFA World Cup (2018), the IIHF World Championships (2016–2019, 2021), the IIHF World Junior Championship (2019), and every Gagarin Cup Final since 2017.

Her work has appeared in leading Russian sports outlets like Championat.com and Sport24, as well as on the official websites of the KHL and the Women’s Hockey League (WHL). Daria has conducted exclusive interviews with some of the sport’s most recognized names, including Alex Ovechkin, Jaromir Jagr, Kirill Kaprizov, Sergei Bobrovsky, and Igor Shesterkin.

Beyond her writing, Daria brings extensive on-camera experience. She hosted NHL Today on Yandex.Efir and has produced powerful long-form projects such as the documentary Lokomotiv Crash and the series Hockey Country, featuring stars like Ovechkin, Malkin, Bobrovsky, Vasilevskiy, and Panarin. Her work has taken her to NHL games across North America and international events like the NHL Global Series in Europe.

In addition to her media career, Daria is a certified integrative nutritionist with a focus on sports nutrition. She works one-on-one with KHL players, helping them optimize performance and recovery through tailored nutrition plans. Her ability to blend media expertise with athlete support gives her a unique presence in the professional hockey world.

Daria publishes in both English and Russian and is the creator of the Telegram channel Coolest Game on Earth, where she shares insights, interviews, and behind-the-scenes stories from the hockey world.
